agent_authored.description: OSIRIS is a fully relativistic electromagnetic particle-in-cell code for kinetic plasma simulations. It couples charged-particle dynamics to self-consistent electromagnetic fields and provides collisions, ionization, restart, load balancing, and scientific diagnostics for plasma-physics and plasma-based-accelerator studies.

modules.title: OSIRIS
modules.expensive_path: The coupled PIC iteration advances particle phase-space state, deposits charge-conserving currents, updates electromagnetic fields, exchanges guard cells across MPI domains, and writes diagnostics; particle push and deposition scale with particle count while field updates and communication scale with grid size and decomposition.
modules.rationale: OSIRIS has one configure/Make build, one dimension-specific program entry point, one coupled simulation state, and one family of input decks. Particle, current, field, collision, diagnostic, restart, and load-balancing directories are internal algorithm stages rather than independently executable packages with separate scientific input/output contracts and official suites, so the whole-codebase default is the coherent module boundary.
hazards: A native build requires an external Fortran compiler, MPI wrappers, and HDF5 Fortran libraries; they were unavailable on the investigation host.

Particle initialization and some physics models use pseudorandom generators; fixed seeds are available, but results can vary with MPI decomposition unless decomposition-independent RNG behavior is enabled.
The repository supplies official example decks but no checked-in numerical golden outputs or standalone regression harness.
Particle storage order, MPI rank layout, timings, and metadata are not stable scientific identities and must not be compared positionally in later checks.
modules.purpose: Advance relativistic kinetic plasma species and self-consistent electromagnetic fields in one coupled particle-in-cell simulation, with production diagnostics and parallel execution.
primary_inputs: An OSIRIS text input deck selecting dimensionality-compatible grid, time step, species, distribution, field, boundary, solver, diagnostic, restart, and parallel-decomposition parameters
Optional raw particle inputs or restart files for workflows that request them
Compile-time dimension and system configuration selected through the configure script
primary_outputs: HDF5 or ZDF scientific diagnostics for fields, currents, particle species, phase space, and derived quantities
Runtime logs, build/run metadata, and timing profiles
algorithm_stages: Parse the input deck, initialize MPI, grids, fields, particle species, random generators, diagnostics, and optional restart state
Advance charged particles and deposit currents and charge
Update electromagnetic fields and exchange distributed guard cells
Apply configured collisions, ionization, boundaries, smoothing, and moving-window operations
Write diagnostics and restart data, report load, and optionally rebalance MPI domains
unique_responsibilities: Own the complete coupled PIC state and time-integration loop
Provide 1D, 2D, and 3D dimension-specific executables from one source tree
Provide the input-deck language and diagnostic formats used by all bundled examples
not_responsible_for: Post-processing or visualization beyond the bundled example notebook
Supplying a standalone automated regression harness or checked-in numerical golden outputs
Providing the external Fortran, MPI, HDF5, FFTW, PAPI, or SIONlib toolchains
modules.differences: This is the single whole-codebase module. Particle, current, electromagnetic-field, collision, I/O, diagnostic, restart, and load-balancing directories are internal stages and have no independent build, entry point, or official suite.
modules.classification: agent-authored module card; CLI-computed size and approval status

official_tests.summary: The repository contains 13 OSIRIS input decks: three base decks and ten additional examples covering wakefield acceleration, exact particle pushing, custom-solver use, and raw-particle workflows. It contains no checked-in numerical golden outputs.
